title: BNCI 2024-001 Handwritten Character Classification dataset
description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants who wrote ten letters (a, d, e, f, j, n, o, s, t, v) with the right index finger after a visual cue. The dataset supports classification of handwritten characters, either directly from low-frequency and broadband EEG or with a two-step approach that first decodes continuous hand kinematics and then classifies the letter. It is intended for research on non-invasive brain-computer interfaces for communication.
methods_description: 60-channel active-electrode EEG plus 4 EOG channels were recorded with BrainVision amplifiers at 500 Hz, referenced to the right mastoid. Each trial lasted 8.5 s: the letter faded in for 2 s, stayed visible for 0.5 s and faded out for 2 s, followed by a 4 s writing phase. Each letter was written 60 times across 15 runs. Preprocessing included notch and bandpass filtering, EOG correction, ICA, common average referencing, bad-segment rejection and downsampling to 128 Hz.
